answer: In an agent economy that pays scouts to wander through karst caves and map relic sites, each agent must bond funds, and paid jobs are allocated in proportion to bonded stake. Splitting one bond among a thousand fake identities gives the attacker the same total chance of winning work as one identity. To capture more jobs, the attacker must lock up more capital for the full job period, sacrificing its use elsewhere; creating accounts alone buys no advantage.
